title: Material Behavior in Sales
purpose: Explain how product and master-data choices change Sales execution without pretending that every behavior is a separate business process.
lead_rule: Do not stop at material type. Ask which master-data setting changes item behavior, ATP, delivery, procurement, production, billing, warehouse execution, or traceability.
decision_path: Does the item have a structure or configuration?
Does logistics need batch, serial, packaging, or HU identity?
Who owns the stock while it is outside the plant?
Which downstream process changes because of this master-data choice?

behavior_profiles.title: Standard / Stock Material
behavior_profiles.business_question: Is the item fulfilled from available or planned own stock?
activation_data: Sales views and item category group
sales_effects: Normal item-category and schedule-line logic can make the item ATP and delivery relevant.
Plant and stock situation influence the promise date and fulfillment path.
Billing normally follows the configured order or delivery flow.
lead_questions: Which product field changes the item category or schedule line?
Is the item really stock fulfilled, or does procurement or production create supply?
Which plant and ATP scope own the promise?

behavior_profiles.title: Service / Non-stock
behavior_profiles.memory_hook: Sell value without pretending every line must leave a warehouse.
behavior_profiles.business_question: Is the commercial item a service or non-stock item, and where is execution recorded?
activation_data: Service product or service material setup
Item category group such as DIEN in classic scenarios
sales_effects: The item can be priced and billed without normal stock fulfillment.
Physical delivery and stock ATP can be absent depending on the item design.
Execution may be owned by Sales, Service, or procurement depending on the solution scope.
lead_questions: Are we selling a commercial service line or managing service execution in SAP Service?
What is the billing trigger: order, confirmation, time and material, milestone, or another rule?
Do external resources or purchased services create a procurement dependency?

behavior_profiles.title: Sales BOM / Kit
behavior_profiles.memory_hook: One sellable product can explode into a main item and components.
behavior_profiles.business_question: Does the commercial structure behave at main-item level or component level?
activation_data: Item-category determination for main item and subitems
sales_effects: Main-item versus component ownership changes pricing, ATP, delivery, and document structure.
Higher-level and subitem categories become part of the runtime control model.
Make-to-order can connect the sold structure to production, but that is a separate supply decision.
lead_questions: Is pricing controlled by the kit or by its components?
Must all components be available before the kit can be promised or delivered?
Is this only a commercial structure, or does production consume the structure too?

behavior_profiles.title: Configurable Material
behavior_profiles.memory_hook: The sales order can carry the choices that shape what gets built.
behavior_profiles.business_question: Does customer configuration influence components, routing, price, or production?
activation_data: BOM and routing where production follows
sales_effects: The order captures characteristic values and a configuration result.
Configuration can select components and production data.
Pricing and availability can depend on the selected characteristics or components.
lead_questions: Which choices are commercial and which choices change engineering or production?
When is the configuration fixed, and what happens after a later change?
Which BOM and routing are selected for the configured result?

behavior_profiles.title: Packaging Material / Handling Unit
behavior_profiles.memory_hook: The box or pallet becomes part of logistics execution, not decoration around the product.
behavior_profiles.business_question: Does fulfillment need an explicit packing object that groups goods with packaging material?
activation_data: Packing rules or packaging specifications where used
Handling Unit and warehouse integration settings
sales_effects: Delivery quantities can be packed into Handling Units.
The packing hierarchy becomes relevant for picking, loading, warehouse, and transport execution.
Packaging identity is different from ownership of returnable packaging stock.
lead_questions: Is packaging consumed, tracked, returned, or charged?
Where is packing decided: delivery, EWM, packing instruction, or another rule?
Which downstream system needs the HU identity and hierarchy?

behavior_profiles.title: Returnable Packaging
behavior_profiles.memory_hook: The crate can leave the plant while ownership stays with the company.
behavior_profiles.business_question: Do reusable pallets, crates, or containers remain company-owned while held by the customer?
activation_data: Return, charge, or settlement rules where required
sales_effects: Customer-held packaging is reconciled separately from normal sold goods.
Return or pickup reduces the open customer-held quantity.
Charging for missing or retained packaging is a separate commercial decision.
lead_questions: Who owns the packaging at every step?
How do we reconcile the customer-held balance and aging?
When do we request return and when do we charge the customer?

behavior_profiles.title: Batch-managed Material
behavior_profiles.memory_hook: Quantity is not enough; batch identity matters.
behavior_profiles.business_question: Must Sales and fulfillment distinguish stock by batch attributes, status, or shelf life?
activation_data: Batch determination or selection strategy where used
Classification, status, shelf-life, and selection rules where relevant
sales_effects: Delivery execution can require selection or determination of a valid batch.
Traceability continues through delivery, warehouse, returns, and quality processes.
Physically existing stock may still be unusable because its batch attributes do not satisfy the requirement.
lead_questions: Is the batch selected in the order, delivery, or warehouse?
Which attributes can make an available batch unacceptable?
How are batch substitutions and returns traced?

behavior_profiles.title: Serial-managed Material
behavior_profiles.memory_hook: Each physical unit can need its own identity.
behavior_profiles.business_question: Does the process need to know the exact physical unit that was delivered, returned, or serviced?
activation_data: Equipment or service integration where relevant
sales_effects: Execution can require serial-number assignment before goods issue.
Returns and service can identify the exact sold unit rather than only product and quantity.
Serialization mainly changes logistics and after-sales traceability, not the commercial price by itself.
lead_questions: At which process step is serial assignment mandatory?
Does the serial number create or connect to equipment or an installed base?
How is the exact returned unit matched to the original delivery?

industry_extensions.title: Empties / Full Products
industry_extensions.use_when: Beverage or deposit-driven logistics models full goods and reusable empties as linked products.
industry_extensions.why_not_core: Useful, but industry-specific. Keep it below the universal material-behavior layer.
